name: Lorde
description:
'''Ella Marija Lani Yelich-O'Connor''' (born 7 November 1996), known professionally as '''Lorde''' ({{IPAc-en|l|ɔr|d}} {{respell|LORD}}), is a New Zealand singer-songwriter. An influential figure in [[alternative pop]] music, she is known for her unconventional production style and introspective songwriting.

Lorde first gained recognition as a teenager during a talent show performance. After signing with [[Universal Music Group]] (UMG), she began working with producer [[Joel Little]] and released the [[extended play]] (EP) ''[[The Love Club EP]]'' (2012). Her debut single, "[[Royals (song)|Royals]]", topped the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], won two [[Grammy Awards]], and became one of the [[best-selling singles]] of all time. Her debut studio album, ''[[Pure Heroine]]'' (2013), achieved further critical acclaim and commercial success. The following year, Lorde curated [[The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1 (soundtrack)|the soundtrack]] for the 2014 film ''[[The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1]].''

Lorde collaborated with producer [[Jack Antonoff]] on her next album, ''[[Melodrama (Lorde album)|Melodrama]]'' (2017), which debuted atop the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] and has since been ranked among of the "[[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time|500 Greatest Albums of All Time]]" by ''[[Rolling Stone]]''. She explored [[indie folk]] and [[Psychedelic music|psychedelic]] styles on her third studio album, ''[[Solar Power (album)|Solar Power]]'' (2021), before returning to an [[Electronic music|electronic]]-oriented sound for her fourth studio album, ''[[Virgin (Lorde album)|Virgin]]'' (2025).

[[List of awards and nominations received by Lorde|Lorde's accolades]] include 20 [[Aotearoa Music Awards]], two Grammy Awards, two [[Brit Awards]], a [[Taite Music Prize]] and a nomination for a [[Golden Globe Award]]. She appeared in ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]''{{'}}s list of the most influential teenagers in 2013 and 2014, and the 2014 edition of [[Forbes 30 Under 30|''Forbes'' 30 Under 30]]. In addition to her solo work, she has co-written songs for other artists, including [[Broods]] and [[Bleachers (band)|Bleachers]].
